correctness.rationale: For c>=5 every q in (c/2,c] has v_q(c!)=1 because q^2>c. Exact Legendre parity computes s(1!)..s(10!)=(1,2,6,6,30,5,35,70,70,7). The direct prime count for 11<=c<=50 is at least 2; for c>=51 Nagura at x=c/2 and x=5c/6 yields disjoint q1 in (c/2,3c/5), q2 in (5c/6,c); both divide s(c!), so it is composite. Independent integer program recomputed kernels through 199 and c=11..50 windows. This proves exactly c=2,6,10, not merely a finite observation.
residual_risks: An unindexed elementary argument could also combine prime intervals and the finite boundary.
The Yudin manuscript was available as title and abstract, not complete text: Oxford institutional access returned vpn_disconnected after arXiv/PDF/OA attempts.
The finite check does not prove the tail, which relies on the published prime interval theorem.
